+---
+name: openheritage-catalog-review
+description: Review existing OpenHeritage Sources and canonical places on behalf of a signed-in member and correct or complete them from evidence — coverage dates and places, classification tags, repository references, translations, place names, parents and identifiers — with the member's Personal API token. Use when a member asks their agent to check, fix or backfill catalogue records. Use openheritage-source-import to create new Sources and openheritage-archives for read-only research.
+metadata:
+  version: 1.0.0
+---
+
+# OpenHeritage Catalog Review
+
+Help a member keep the shared catalogue correct. You work as that member: every
+change carries their name in the record's history, and readers see the result
+at once. Write only what the evidence proves, in the words a careful archivist
+would use, and leave everything else to the member's report.
+
+Read [references/source-review.md](references/source-review.md) before the
+first Source change and [references/place-review.md](references/place-review.md)
+before the first place change. Use `openheritage-archives` for reading
+documents and pages.
+
+## Safety and setup
+
+~~~bash
+BASE="\${OPENHERITAGE_BASE_URL:-https://openheritage.online}"
+AUTH="Authorization: Bearer $OPENHERITAGE_API_TOKEN"
+UA="User-Agent: <agent-name>/<version> (catalog review)"
+~~~
+
+- Ask the member to create a Personal API token at
+  `https://openheritage.online/{locale}/profile/api-tokens` with `api:sources`
+  (Sources), plus `api:places` only when place changes are wanted. Never ask
+  for `api:destructive`: this workflow never deletes.
+- Send the token only as `Authorization: Bearer $OPENHERITAGE_API_TOKEN`. Never
+  put it in a URL, file, log, checkpoint or report, and never send it to MCP.
+  MCP (`https://openheritage.online/mcp`) is anonymous: use it for search only.
+- Start with `GET /api/users/me/identity` to learn which account and scopes the
+  token carries. Read the live operation schemas at `$BASE/api/openapi/v1.json`
+  (`x-api-required-scopes`) before the first write.
+- A token always acts as a plain member, even when its owner is a moderator. It
+  cannot approve, verify, merge, restore or match "Places to match" entries.
+- Send a descriptive `User-Agent`; a bare client may be blocked.
+- Never use `/api/admin/*`. Never delete, unlink a document, change a Source's
+  type or visibility, or remove a fact you cannot show to be wrong.
+
+## What you may change
+
+| Record | Your agent may write | Otherwise |
+|---|---|---|
+| Sources the member created | any field except as below | — |
+| Other members' `archive-case` Sources that are `public` and `Pending` or `Approved` | content fields; never `type` or `visibility` | 403: report it |
+| `Rejected`, private, limited or non-public Sources of others; other Source types | nothing | report the proposed correction |
+| Canonical places | names, types, parents, point, existence dates, external ids, reference links | merges, deletions, verification: report for moderators |
+
+Consequences to tell the member before the first such write:
+
+- A change to an `Approved` Source by someone who cannot approve sources sends
+  it back to `Pending`, and the review status is public ("not reviewed yet").
+- A change to a `Verified` place by a member resets it to `Unverified` until a
+  moderator verifies it again.
+
+Count both in the report.
+
+## Nothing technical in OpenHeritage data
+
+Every field you write is catalogue content for a reader of the record. Never
+write into any field — descriptions, `scopeNote`, link `note` or `label`,
+`unresolved.note`, place notes, provenance `citation`, change summaries:
+
+- that an agent or AI made or checked the change, or for whom;
+- how a fact was found (OCR, the page you read it on, search steps, tool or
+  model names), confidence, doubt, "probably", "needs review", TODOs;
+- timestamps, run or batch ids, checkpoint data, or text addressed to
+  moderators.
+
+A published citation or the archive's own catalogue URL is content and goes in
+`referenceLinks` or the repository link. "Found on page 3 by OCR" is not. What
+you checked, why you changed it, what stayed uncertain and what you skipped
+belongs in the report to the member, and only there. A fact that needs a caveat
+to be true is not proven: leave the field alone and report it.
+
+## Which Sources, in what order
+
+Agree the scope with the member first: their research, an archive, a fund or a
+place. Then build a queue with `GET /api/sources` (paged mode, `skip=0`,
+`limit` ≤ 100). Unknown parameter *names* are ignored silently, so confirm each
+name below in the live OpenAPI document before trusting a filtered result.
+
+| Parameter | Use |
+|---|---|
+| `approvalStatus=Pending` | the normal target |
+| `missing=coverage-dates\|coverage-places\|place-link\|tags\|repository-reference` (repeatable, all must hold) | a specific gap |
+| `minMissing=2` | Sources with several gaps at once |
+| `hasDocuments=true` / `hasLinks=true` | something to check the record against |
+| `placeId` + `includeDescendants=true`, `yearFrom`, `yearTo` | the member's research area |
+| `repositoryId`, `query` | one archive; a fund or title |
+| `createdAfter`, `createdBefore`, `updatedAfter`, `updatedBefore` | ISO 8601 instants |
+| `sortBy=updatedAt&sortDesc=false` | longest untouched first |
+
+1. **Research interest.** Read the member's own research projects
+   (`GET /api/researches?onlyMine=true`, then each `GET /api/researches/{id}`):
+   places with `canonicalPlaceId`, years and surnames. Turn them into `placeId`
+   with `includeDescendants=true` and `yearFrom`/`yearTo`. Sources without a
+   coverage place cannot match a place filter: reach them through the
+   repositories of the Sources you matched and a `query` for the place names.
+   With no research projects, ask the member for the archive, fund or place.
+2. **Priority tiers**, each `approvalStatus=Pending`, `minMissing=2` before `1`:
+   1. `hasDocuments=true` — the pages are the evidence;
+   2. `hasDocuments=false&hasLinks=true` — a catalogue page or scan to check;
+   3. Sources with almost no information — last, and usually only reported.
+3. **Order** inside a tier: `sortBy=updatedAt&sortDesc=false`. Continue a run
+   with `updatedAfter=<updatedAt of the last row>` instead of a growing `skip`.
+4. **Leave fresh work alone.** Add `updatedBefore=<now − 2 hours>`, and check
+   `updatedAt` again on the read just before writing: someone may still be
+   editing that Source.
+5. **New arrivals** (optional extra pass):
+   `createdAfter=<now − 3 days>&createdBefore=<now − 1 day>&approvalStatus=Pending`.
+6. Touch an `Approved` Source only when the member points at it or names its
+   fund.
+
+A 503 with `Retry-After` on a review filter means the search index cannot answer
+now; wait as directed instead of paging the whole catalogue.
+
+~~~bash
+# two hours ago, UTC: GNU date -d '2 hours ago', BSD/macOS date -v-2H
+CUTOFF=$(date -u -d '2 hours ago' +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ 2>/dev/null || date -u -v-2H +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
+curl -sS --get "$BASE/api/sources" -H "$AUTH" -H "$UA" \
+  --data-urlencode "approvalStatus=Pending" --data-urlencode "type=archive-case" \
+  --data-urlencode "hasDocuments=true" --data-urlencode "minMissing=2" \
+  --data-urlencode "placeId=$PLACE_ID" --data-urlencode "includeDescendants=true" \
+  --data-urlencode "updatedBefore=$CUTOFF" \
+  --data-urlencode "sortBy=updatedAt" --data-urlencode "sortDesc=false" \
+  --data-urlencode "skip=0" --data-urlencode "limit=50" \
+  | jq '.items[] | {id, title, approvalStatus, updatedAt, documentCount}'
+~~~
+
+## Workflow
+
+1. **Agree scope and limits** with the member: which records, which fields,
+   whether `Approved` Sources and `Verified` places may be touched, and how
+   many records per run.
+2. **Build the queue** as above and keep it in a local checkpoint.
+3. **Read each record fully**: `GET /api/sources/{id}` (keep `version` and
+   `updatedAt`), `GET /api/sources/{id}/revisions` (what others changed and
+   why it looks the way it does), then its documents and pages
+   (`openheritage-archives`, "Reading a source's documents").
+4. **Gather evidence** for each intended change (see the references). No
+   evidence, no write.
+5. **Show the first proposed changes** — field, old value, new value, evidence —
+   for the first few records and wait for the member's go-ahead. Continue
+   without asking only within what the member approved.
+6. **Write** one record at a time: `PATCH /api/sources/{id}` with the `version`
+   you read and only the fields you change; `PUT /api/canonical-places/{id}`
+   with the whole place. Never `PUT` a Source.
+7. **Read back** and compare with what you sent. A change that does nothing
+   returns the same `version`.
+8. **Checkpoint** the record id, the new version and the next action.
+9. **Report** at the end (see below).
+
+## Stop and ask
+
+Stop writing and ask the member when:
+
+- 401, or 403 on a record you expected to be editable (the rights changed or
+  the token lacks a scope);
+- several candidates fit a place, an archive or a duplicate Source;
+- the evidence contradicts what another member wrote recently (a revision of
+  the last weeks): report it rather than overwrite;
+- a change would remove information rather than add or correct it;
+- the record is outside the agreed scope.
+
+## Rate limits and request pacing
+
+- Keep one request in flight. Read a record, decide, write, read back, then
+  move on; never crawl a repository or prefetch whole documents.
+- Use the narrowest filters and a small page; prefer `search_page_text` (MCP)
+  or `GET /api/search` with `entityTypes=page` to reading pages in sequence.
+- On 429, stop issuing calls. Honor Retry-After or `X-RateLimit-Reset`; otherwise use full-jitter backoff with ceilings of 1, 2, then 4 seconds and make at most three retries.
+- Do not automatically retry 409 or 422. On 409 re-read the record and apply
+  your change again only if it still fits; on 422 correct the request from the
+  `errors` it names. Retry a mutation after 429 only with explicit user intent; never retry an unkeyed mutation.
+- After an unknown outcome (timeout, dropped connection), read the record
+  before deciding whether the write happened.
+
+## Report to the member
+
+Keep it in the conversation or a local file the member chooses, never in
+OpenHeritage. For each record: link
+(`https://openheritage.online/{locale}/sources/{id}` or `/places/{id}`), what
+changed (old → new), the evidence, and what you left alone and why. Then totals:
+records read, changed, unchanged, skipped (403, out of scope, no evidence);
+Sources returned to review; places reset to Unverified; proposed corrections
+the member or a moderator must make (duplicates, merges, rejected or private
+Sources, taxonomy gaps, missing repositories)."},{"sha":"7e6b9dc21248d36001b24a2888447f94420a79aa","filename":"skills/openheritage-catalog-review/references/place-review.md","status":"added","additions":123,"deletions":0,"changes":123,"blob_url":"https://github.com/OpenHeritageOnline/agent-tooling/blob/e26fcca8361080d5a94b0d1f9f92c8fbf47283d9/skills%2Fopenheritage-catalog-review%2Freferences%2Fplace-review.md","raw_url":"https://github.com/OpenHeritageOnline/agent-tooling/raw/e26fcca8361080d5a94b0d1f9f92c8fbf47283d9/skills%2Fopenheritage-catalog-review%2Freferences%2Fplace-review.md","contents_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/OpenHeritageOnline/agent-tooling/contents/skills%2Fopenheritage-catalog-review%2Freferences%2Fplace-review.md?ref=e26fcca8361080d5a94b0d1f9f92c8fbf47283d9","patch":"@@ -0,0 +1,123 @@
+# Reviewing a canonical place
+
+A canonical place is OpenHeritage's gazetteer entry for a settlement or an
+administrative, church or historical area, with its names over time, types,
+parents, point, outline and external identifiers. Sources, photos and
+researches link to it. Changing a place changes what every linked record shows,
+so the bar is higher than for a Source.
+
+## Find before anything
+
+Name-based creation has no duplicate check, so search every way before deciding
+a place is missing or wrong:
+
+| GET | Use |
+|---|---|
+| `/api/canonical-places?query=…&date=YYYY-MM-DD&typeCode=…&skip=0&take=50` | names in every language; `date` resolves names, types and parents as of that day |
+| `/api/canonical-places/by-external-identity?provider=wikidata&externalId=Q…` | `wikidata`, `katotth`, `koatuu`, `osm-node`, `osm-way`, `osm-relation`, `geonames` |
+| `/api/canonical-places/nearby?latitude=…&longitude=…&radiusKm=…` | places near a point |
+| `/api/canonical-places/at-point?latitude=…&longitude=…` | outlines containing a point, innermost first |
+| `/api/canonical-places/{id}?date=YYYY-MM-DD` | one place, resolved for a date |
+| `/api/canonical-places/{id}/children` | what lies under it |
+| `/api/canonical-places/{id}/revisions` | who changed what; read before changing |
+| `/api/place-types` | the type codes in use |
+| `/api/osm/places?q=…&limit=10&language=uk` | OpenStreetMap settlements and areas, to create a missing place |
+
+Places can also be searched anonymously through MCP (`search_places`,
+`autocomplete_places`, `find_places_nearby`, `get_place`).
+
+## Creating a missing place
+
+Only from an OpenStreetMap pick: `POST /api/canonical-places/from-osm` with
+`{"osmType": "node|way|relation", "osmId": 123}`. The server reads the element
+itself, reuses a place that already carries that OSM id, accepts settlements
+and administrative areas only, and creates it `Unverified`. Creation is rate
+limited (about 30 an hour). A place OSM does not know (a vanished village, a
+historical повіт) is not created by this workflow: keep the name on the Source
+with `unresolved` and report it.
+
+## Changing a place: PUT is the whole state
+
+~~~bash
+curl -sS "$BASE/api/canonical-places/$PLACE_ID" -H "$AUTH" -H "$UA" > place.json
+# edit a copy, then:
+curl -sS -X PUT "$BASE/api/canonical-places/$PLACE_ID" -H "$AUTH" -H "$UA" \
+  -H "Content-Type: application/json" --data @place-update.json
+~~~
+
+- `version` is required; a stale one is 409.
+- A collection you leave out or send as `null` (`names`, `typeAssignments`,
+  `relations`, `externalIdentities`, `referenceLinks`, `notes`, `geometries`)
+  is left alone. A collection you send is the **complete** list: items without
+  `id` are added, items with a stored `id` are updated, and stored items whose
+  `id` you leave out are **deleted**. So send only the collections you change,
+  each with every stored item and its `id`.
+- `point`, `existenceFrom`, `existenceUntil` are replaced when sent; clear them
+  only with `clearPoint`, `clearExistenceFrom`, `clearExistenceUntil`, and only
+  when the stored value is shown to be wrong.
+- A member's change to a `Verified` place sets it to `Unverified` ("not
+  reviewed yet") until a moderator verifies it again. Make such a change only
+  on strong evidence, and list every such place in the report.
+- Use exactly these values. An unknown name `kind` or `relationType` is
+  refused with 422; an unknown `category` becomes `Other` and an unknown
+  `confidence` is dropped, so check those two before sending.
+  - name `kind`: `Official`, `Common`, `Historical`, `Exonym`, `Endonym`,
+    `Church`, `Transliteration`, `SourceMention`, `Other`;
+  - `relationType`: `AdministrativeParent`, `EcclesiasticalParent`,
+    `GeographicParent`, `HistoricalParent`, `PoliticalSovereignty`,
+    `MilitaryOccupation`, `CivilOccupation`, `ClaimedSovereignty`,
+    `ContestedControl`, `Predecessor`, `Successor`, `Other`;
+  - reference link `category`: `OfficialSite`, `SocialGroup`, `ArchiveCatalog`,
+    `Article`, `Map`, `Tourism`, `ChurchSite`, `CemeterySite`, `CommunityWiki`,
+    `Other`;
+  - provenance `confidence`: `Definite`, `Probable`, `Possible`, `Speculative`.
+
+~~~json
+{
+  "version": 12,
+  "names": [
+    { "id": "${STORED_NAME_ID}", "value": "Кропивницький", "languageCode": "uk",
+      "kind": "Official", "isPreferred": true, "dateWindows": [{ "type": "after", "value": "2016-07-14" }] },
+    { "value": "Єлисаветград", "languageCode": "uk", "kind": "Historical", "isPreferred": false,
+      "dateWindows": [{ "type": "range", "value": "1784/1924" }],
+      "provenance": { "citation": "${PUBLISHED_WORK_AND_PAGE}", "sourceUrl": "${PUBLISHED_URL}" } }
+  ]
+}
+~~~
+
+## Names
+
+- Exactly one preferred name in the whole list; every name has a value and a
+  language code.
+- Add a historical name with the years it was used (`dateWindows`) and a
+  citation of the published work or record it comes from. The citation names
+  that work; it never says how you found it.
+- Never derive or transliterate a form yourself, and never add a Russian form
+  derived from another language. A Russian name is added only as `Historical`
+  or `SourceMention` with a citation, exactly as a record writes it, and is
+  never preferred.
+- Do not rename a place to match a Source's spelling: the Source keeps its
+  spelling in its own coverage `name`.
+
+## Parents, types, points, identifiers
+
+- Parents (`AdministrativeParent`, `EcclesiasticalParent`, …) carry the years
+  they held. Before adding one, read the parent's own chain upward: the server
+  rejects only a place that is its own parent, not longer cycles.
+- Types come from `/api/place-types`; give a type the years it held when it
+  changed (a village that became a town).
+- Set or move a point only from the place's own outline, an authority record
+  (Wikidata, KATOTTH, OSM) or a published map, with that source in the
+  provenance; never from a Source's coverage or a guess.
+- Add an external id only when the authority record clearly describes this
+  place (name, location, type). The same id on two places means a duplicate:
+  report it, do not move the id.
+
+## Report, do not fix
+
+Duplicates, wrong merges, a place that should be deleted, wrong verification,
+and "Places to match" decisions are moderators' work. Report them to the member
+with both place links and the evidence. A member may suggest a place for a
+"Places to match" entry (`POST /api/unresolved-places/{id}/suggestions` with
+`{"placeId": "…"}`, `note` left empty or a fact from the record) when the
+member asked for it."},{"sha":"5ecf5d817d874c9e3760296ed70ab4090560b591","filename":"skills/openheritage-catalog-review/references/source-review.md","status":"added","additions":160,"deletions":0,"changes":160,"blob_url":"https://github.com/OpenHeritageOnline/agent-tooling/blob/e26fcca8361080d5a94b0d1f9f92c8fbf47283d9/skills%2Fopenheritage-catalog-review%2Freferences%2Fsource-review.md","raw_url":"https://github.com/OpenHeritageOnline/agent-tooling/raw/e26fcca8361080d5a94b0d1f9f92c8fbf47283d9/skills%2Fopenheritage-catalog-review%2Freferences%2Fsource-review.md","contents_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/OpenHeritageOnline/agent-tooling/contents/skills%2Fopenheritage-catalog-review%2Freferences%2Fsource-review.md?ref=e26fcca8361080d5a94b0d1f9f92c8fbf47283d9","patch":"@@ -0,0 +1,160 @@
+# Reviewing a Source
+
+Field-by-field checks for an existing Source. The creation rules and full JSON
+shapes are in `openheritage-source-import` (`references/source-model.md`); this
+file says what to check and how to change it without losing anything.
+
+## Evidence
+
+Use, in this order:
+
+1. the Source's own pages: the case cover, title page, first and last register
+   pages, the inventory line pasted inside the cover;
+2. the holding archive's finding aid or catalogue page for that unit (its
+   repository link `url`, or the archive's site);
+3. the Source's existing reference links (Wikisource, FamilySearch, a printed
+   catalogue).
+
+Never use memory, analogy with a neighbouring case, or a pattern of reference
+codes as evidence. A fact stated only in another OpenHeritage record is a lead
+to check, not proof. When sources disagree, write nothing and report both.
+
+## Changing a Source: PATCH
+
+~~~bash
+curl -sS -X PATCH "$BASE/api/sources/$SOURCE_ID" -H "$AUTH" -H "$UA" \
+  -H "Content-Type: application/json" --data @patch.json
+~~~
+
+- Send `version` (as read) and only the fields you change; everything left out
+  keeps what is stored.
+- An array you send **replaces** the stored set; `[]` clears it. To add one
+  coverage segment, tag or link, send the full stored array plus the addition,
+  each stored item unchanged (keep every `canonicalPlaceId`, `unresolvedPlaceId`,
+  point and name).
+- A stale `version` is 409: re-read and decide again.
+- Validation failures are 422 `validation_failed` with field-addressed
+  `errors`; fix the body, do not retry it unchanged.
+
+~~~json
+{
+  "version": 7,
+  "coverageSegments": [
+    {
+      "dateWindows": [{ "type": "range", "value": "1850/1875" }],
+      "locations": [
+        { "name": "Єлисаветград", "canonicalPlaceId": "${PLACE_ID}" }
+      ]
+    }
+  ]
+}
+~~~
+
+## Coverage
+
+- `originDate` is when the Source itself was made; coverage is the dates and
+  places its content is about. Do not copy one into the other.
+- Date expressions: `exact` (`1897`, `1897-04`, `1897-04-23`), `approximate`,
+  `before`, `after`, `range` (`1897/1902`). Never turn a range into an exact
+  date; omit what the evidence does not bound.
+- **Fewest segments.** Each place appears once, its years merged into
+  contiguous ranges (several date windows on one segment for gaps — never fill
+  a gap), and places sharing exactly the same periods share one segment. Never
+  one segment per year. When adding to existing coverage, merge and collapse
+  the stored and new coverage together.
+- **Names stay as written.** A location's `name` is the place as the Source
+  names it (Єлисаветград, not Кропивницький; a village as the register spells
+  it). The canonical place supplies the link and the point; it never replaces
+  the name. Do not translate or modernise a name.
+- Add `canonicalPlaceId` only when exactly one active place fits the name,
+  the date and the area the Source gives (повіт, parish, gubernia). Search with
+  the Source's date (`GET /api/canonical-places?query=…&date=1870-01-01`).
+- Otherwise keep the name and send
+  `unresolved: {area, reason: ambiguous|vanished|renamed|other, candidates, note}`
+  so it joins the shared "Places to match" queue, where moderators decide.
+  `area` is the administrative context the Source prints; `candidates` are
+  place ids that fit; `note` stays empty unless it states a fact from the
+  Source (e.g. the parish), never your process.
+- Never add coordinates you inferred. A point comes from the canonical place.
+- A metrical book is written in one parish church: the villages its parish
+  served are coverage locations, not authors.
+
+## Repository references
+
+- Link an existing repository (`GET /api/repositories?query=…`,
+  `GET /api/repositories/{id}`); never create one in this workflow. If the
+  holder is not on OpenHeritage, report it.
+- The archive code is fund–opys–case joined by hyphens, as the case cover
+  stamps it (`227-2-1366`), the fund keeping its letter prefix in the form
+  sibling Sources of that fund use (`Р8985-1-194`). Check a few Sources of the
+  same fund (`repositoryId` + `sortBy=reference`) for the house form and the
+  repository's `referenceCodeRegexRules` before writing.
+- When a catalogue prints another form (`ф. 227, оп. 1 т. 2, спр. 1366`), keep
+  the cover code as the primary link and add the catalogue form as a second,
+  non-primary link in the same repository, its `note` quoting the printed
+  citation.
+- A link to an archive unit carries the unit's page on the archive's own site
+  in `url`. Fill a missing URL on the existing link; never overwrite a
+  different URL, never add a second link for the same unit.
+- `referenceType` and `accessType` values are lower case (`archive-signature`,
+  `dgs`, `call-number`, `other`; `physical`, `digital`, `hybrid`).
+- Before adding or changing a code, look it up:
+  `GET /api/sources/repository-links?repositoryId=…&referenceCode=…`. Updates
+  have no duplicate check. If another Source already holds the code, do not
+  change either: report the pair as a possible duplicate.
+
+## Classification tags
+
+- Read the tree once: `GET /api/tags/tree?entityType=source`. Select by stable
+  `code`; use the UUID of that environment. A usable tag is active, selectable,
+  applicable to `source` and not a facet root; at most 32 per Source.
+- Add a tag only for what the material shows (a metrical book, a confession
+  list, a revision tale). Type, repository, language, author and place have
+  their own fields: never tag them.
+- Remove a tag only when the material shows it is wrong.
+- A concept missing from the taxonomy is a report item; tags cannot be created
+  with a token.
+
+## Title, descriptions and translations
+
+- The original title and description stay in the language the Source prints
+  them in, Russian included: a Russian original stays the original, never
+  replaced by a translation. Members cannot move an original to another
+  language; the API refuses it.
+- You may add translations in other languages as `human` versions, Ukrainian
+  and English first, when they are missing:
+
+  ~~~json
+  {
+    "version": 7,
+    "titleVersions": {
+      "ru": { "text": "Метрическая книга …", "kind": "original" },
+      "uk": { "text": "Метрична книга …", "kind": "human", "from": "ru" },
+      "en": { "text": "Metrical book …", "kind": "human", "from": "ru" }
+    }
+  }
+  ~~~
+
+  Send every stored version back unchanged beside the new ones.
+- Never create a Russian translation, and never derive a Russian form of a
+  name. Names of people and places, archival references and quotations inside
+  a translation stay as printed.
+- A translation renders the stored original only: it adds no facts and is
+  never evidence for another field. Add translations to Sources you are already
+  reviewing; a missing translation alone does not put a Source in your queue.
+- Correct a title only from the case cover or the archive's catalogue, keeping
+  its wording; do not "improve" style.
+
+## Authors
+
+Change author credits only with clear evidence (a printed compiler, the parish
+church that kept a register) and an existing Author
+(`GET /api/authors?query=…`). Creating Authors needs `api:authors` and is
+outside this workflow: report the missing Author.
+
+## Read-back checklist
+
+After each `PATCH`, `GET /api/sources/{id}` and check: the new `version`; every
+field you sent; every stored item of each array you sent is still there; no
+`canonicalPlaceId` was lost; `approvalStatus` (Pending after a change to an
+Approved Source); and that no field holds anything but catalogue content."},{"sha":"9dd2d98b6273ea317266362aaa937a238b25fa17","filename":"skills/openheritage-source-import/SKILL.md","status":"modified","additions":2,"deletions":2,"changes":4,"blob_url":"https://github.com/OpenHeritageOnline/agent-tooling/blob/e26fcca8361080d5a94b0d1f9f92c8fbf47283d9/skills%2Fopenheritage-source-import%2FSKILL.md","raw_url":"https://github.com/OpenHeritageOnline/agent-tooling/raw/e26fcca8361080d5a94b0d1f9f92c8fbf47283d9/skills%2Fopenheritage-source-import%2FSKILL.md","contents_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/OpenHeritageOnline/agent-tooling/contents/skills%2Fopenheritage-source-import%2FSKILL.md?ref=e26fcca8361080d5a94b0d1f9f92c8fbf47283d9","patch":"@@ -1,8 +1,8 @@
